title: The camera's part: aperture, shutter, ISO
standards: MA MP-B Standard 5 (lighting, sets and props)
standardsNote: Tom asked for camera settings after the brief; this lesson is an extra (the brief lists five lessons).

steps.text: Lights decide what the picture looks like; the camera decides how bright it comes out. Three settings work together: aperture, shutter speed and ISO. Each full stop doubles or halves the light.
Three-point lighting, with the camera on Auto.
Switch the camera to Manual (under the picture). It starts from Auto's settings, so the meter should read 0. Now make the shutter speed twice as long (for example 1/60 to 1/30).
steps.hint: The Auto / Manual buttons are in the bar under the camera view.
steps.success: The meter moved to +1: one stop brighter.

steps.question: You made the shutter twice as long. What does the meter say now?
steps.explain: Twice as long lets in twice the light: one stop brighter.

steps.text: Get back to correct exposure (meter at 0) WITHOUT changing the shutter: use the aperture instead.
steps.hint: A bigger f-number (for example f/2.8 to f/4) lets in half the light.

steps.question: Which setting also blurs the backdrop more when you change it?
steps.explain: A wide aperture makes the depth of field shallow, so things behind the subject blur.

steps.prompt: You're in a dim room with no extra lights. Which setting would you change first, and what would it cost you?
